decision_maker: Cabinet member for finance and property assets
purpose:
To award a contact for an Enterprise Resource
Planning (Financial Management) System
content:
To use the Government’s
G-Cloud 14 Framework to award a three-year contract to Unit4 for
Software as a Service provision of the Unit4 Enterprise Resource
Planning (ERP) application.  The
contract is for a three-year period commencing 1 October 2026, with
the option to extend for one-year.
 
The cost of the three-year
initial contract period will be £356,520. The optional
one-year extension would be at a cost of £118,840, making the
total contract cost £475,360.  The
costs will be shared equally with Vale of White Horse District
Council.

purpose:
To approve the creation of a
five-year Community Cohesion Strategy and a 2026 -28 work
plan.
content:
To approve the creation of a
five-year Community Cohesion Strategy and a 2026 -28 work
plan.

RESOLVED:
That Cabinet:
a)   
Note the existing community cohesion activity
already being delivered across both councils through the Community
Hub and Be Together programme.

b)   
Approve the development of a five-year community
cohesion strategy that supports the Councils motions for Fair
treatment for all residents (South Oxfordshire District Council, 23
October 2025), and Sanctuary and Fair Treatment for All (Vale of
White Horse District Council, 10 December 2025).

c)    
Note the strategy will finalise a fully funded
action plan for the year 2027/28, linking all existing grant
funding and National Lottery funding into a homogenous action plan.
The strategy action plan will outline in principle further
actions that any future authority can consider
to support community cohesion.

d)   
Approve the commissioning of Belong, a specialist
third-sector organisation with recognised expertise in developing
cohesion strategies that link cultural, social and economic factors
to deliver best practice, to develop a community cohesion strategy
and action for the year 2027/28 for Cabinet approval.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the creation of a five-year Community Cohesion Strategy and a 2026-28 work plan.

content:

councils covering Oxfordshire, Berkshire and Sindon to develop a

b)   
Note the draft indicative funding and resource
allocations for the pre-inception programme.

accountable body for funds received/held on behalf of the

monitoring and assurance arrangements set out in this paper,
including arrangements for the period before a statutory Strategic
Planning Board (SPB) is established through secondary
legislation.

Delegate the detail agreements and working
arrangements for pre-inception development of the SDS to the Deputy
Chief Executive – Place, in consultation with the Director of
Legal and Democratic.


f)     
Note the working arrangements for development of the
SDS.

That Cabinet:

a)   
Approve the updated waste and street cleansing
vehicle selection and procurement policy, which includes the
outlined procurement approach (Appendix 1), and authorises the
Director of Housing and Environment in consultation with the

purpose:
To review and approve options for local plan
making.
content:
RESOLVED:
Cabinet to recommend Council to:

(a) 
agree, subject to the agreement of Vale of White
Horse District Council, preparation of the next Joint Local Plan
for South Oxfordshire and Vale of White Horse districts.

(b) 
agree the principle of governance to prepare this
new joint local plan under Section 15l of the Planning and
Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and to delegate the detailed
arrangements to the Director of Legal and Democratic, in
consultation with the Director of Policy and Programmes and the
Cabinet Members for Planning Policy and Legal and
Democratic.

(c)  
approve formal commencement of the South Oxfordshire
and Vale of White Horse Joint Local Plan 2045, in accordance with
the Town and Country Planning (Local Planning) (England)
Regulations 2026.
 
Subject to Council deciding to accept recommendations (a), (b)
and (c), Cabinet resolved to:
 

(d) 
approve the giving of a Notice of Intention to
commence local plan preparation (see Appendix 1), its publication
on the council’s website and making it available for
inspection.

(e) 
approve the Local Plan Timetable (as set out in
Table 1 of the report), its publication on the council’s
website and making it available for inspection.

(f)   
delegate authority to the Director of Policy and
Programmes, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Planning
Policy, to:
i.                
update and publish the Local Plan Timetable monthly
(or as required) to ensure an up-to-date timetable is publicly
available
ii.               
authorise commencement of a Scoping
Consultation
iii.             
undertake a self-assessment of readiness for local
plan preparation (at Gateway 1) and publish a summary
document
iv.             
approve, submit and publish documents to meet
Gateway 2 (Regulation 26) and Gateway 3 (Regulation 31)
requirements.
v.              
agree the content of and commencement of
consultation on proposed local plan content and evidence
(Regulation 23) and consultation on the proposed local plan
(Regulation 27).

(g) 
If (a) above is not supported, to agree the
preparation and production of a South Oxfordshire Local Plan and to
approve (d) – (f) above in respect of such a plan.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to recommend the Council to prepare the next Joint Local Plan for South Oxfordshire and Vale of White Horse districts.

purpose:
In line with the motion from Full Council, to
review the business case for the council taking devolved powers
from the DVLA to remove, store and dispose of untaxed road
vehicles.
content:
RESOLVED:
 
a)   
That Cabinet reviewed the background on dealing with
untaxed vehicles in South Oxfordshire, together with the perceived
risks and benefits and approved Option 1 - For South Oxfordshire
District Council to take on the devolved duties from the DVLA and
become a Devolved Power Partner (DPP) to remove untaxed road
vehicles within South Oxfordshire, subject to completion of a
procurement process and the establishment of costs by the Head of
Housing and Environment in consultation with the Cabinet member for
Environment.

b)   
To delegate to the Head of Housing and Environment,
working with the Head of Legal and Democratic the authority, in
agreement with the Cabinet member for Environment, to develop an
operationally detailed policy and process for the implementation of
the scheme.

c)   
To delegate to the Head of Legal and Democratic
Services, in consultation with the Head of Housing and Environment,
the authority to sign the Public Service Agreement with the DVLA to
accept the devolved powers, to bring forward any required changes
to the council’s constitution and/or delegated authorities to
enable the council to become a DPP and to enforce the delegated
powers in a fully legal and compliant way.

d)   
To delegate to the Head of Housing and Environment,
in consultation with the Head of Finance, the authority to develop
an operational budget to enable the procurement of a vehicle
removal contractor, and to develop the mechanism for collecting
fees and charges as outlined within this report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to delegate powers to South Oxfordshire District Council to remove untaxed vehicles within the district.

street cleansing vehicles are purchased for use as part of the two
